subject: An exact-local physical Mixer naming adapter retains its issued reference and grants only a verified same-source inverse
question: Can the existing physical Mixer issuer and writer support an owned Aux-name inverse without adopting an Arrange index, importing JSON authority or overwriting a newer name?

reverify.command: In a stopped development fixture, retain the actual Mixer producer's physical Aux source. Populate the existing cache, obtain its reference through readMixer and obtain the current project reference through the existing issuer. Confirm that the issued binding matches the original physical source. Under the existing mutation claim, apply a no-op, refuse stale expected bytes, apply a comma/quote/Unicode name and execute only its actual owned inverse. In a separate sequence, make a second verified name change, refuse the first inverse while that newer name is current, and restore the two actions in their owned order. Independently compare the UI at each exposed boundary and retain original fader and playhead observations.
reverify.expected: No-op grants no inverse; stale expected bytes refuse without a write. Verified writes and inverses retain the same issued physical reference. The older inverse refuses without native calls while the newer name remains current. Lost post-writer authority reports uncertainty rather than exposing the writer's earlier A as current adapter success.
reverify.cost: Two scalar writes in the first sequence and four in the newer-name sequence. No playback, recording, plugin lifecycle, project replacement or save is required.

method: An instrumented development executable linked the actual product module and called the private adapter, its existing resource/project issuers and its existing physical writer. It did not copy the actuator, synthesize an inverse from JSON, add a public route or change the operation registry. Original physical CF identities were retained; diagnostic labels only located the initial source. Independent Accessibility observations compared the host UI. Native wrappers delegated actual setters and paired events and observed only after complete pairs. This development binary includes separate unpublished reader changes and is not a clean publication-build qualification.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record concerns transient physical object custody and exact runtime name bytes, not canonical shipped labels or replacement identity.

observations.what: Actual adapter post-writer proof loss initially exposed the writer's earlier A despite an uncertain typed receipt
observations.counterexample: The real injected channel writer committed the requested name. The adapter's independent post-read then lost operation ownership. No inverse was granted, but the embedded result still reported A. The correction downgrades only that earlier A to B with readback_unavailable, preserves actual before/observed/write_attempted facts, withholds the surviving reference and requires a reread.
observations.limit: These are injected tests, not native proof of authority loss. The initial absent-type compile failure is not a runtime RED. A subsequent test-integrity guard rejected three optional Boolean equality spellings; the assertions were changed to required Boolean values without weakening their conditions.

observations.what: Native Aux action and its actual adapter-owned inverse retained one issued physical reference
A newer actual name prevented the older inverse from posting native calls
observations.limit: The intermediate newer-action inverse was observed by the actual product readback and retained playhead reads, not by a separate UI checkpoint or a full nine-fader census between the two inverse writes.

observations.what: An Aux name duplicated an existing Audio name without importing that other strip's identity
observations.limit: Only this exact physical-object scalar duplicate-name case is observed. No duplicate-name policy, swap scheduling, replacement identity or plan footprint is qualified.

observations.what: An Audio acquisition initially refused after one complete pair; a separately observed already-focused context supported the scalar roundtrip
observations.subsequent_independent_ui: The selected Audio track's Arrange header, background label, inspector track field, inspector strip name and main Mixer name changed together and restored. Selection stayed on that track; other observed names, faders and playhead did not change.
observations.limit: These are two separately issued, freshly observed development actions, not a blind inverse/retry or a cross-process CF identity proof. No product guard was relaxed. The initial acquisition limitation remains; the later success does not isolate its cause. Observing one host coupling does not implement a coupled adapter, verify every required preservation domain or qualify the plan.

observations.what: An actually issued Arrange reference and an unissued project reference could not authorize Mixer writes
observations.limit: This exercises actual existing issuers and the private adapter's accepted-kind/project gates in one stopped fixture. It is not qualification of arbitrary project switches, replacement objects, public routing or planner execution.

conclusion: The existing physical Mixer issuer and bounded writer can support an exact-local adapter-owned inverse on the retained Aux object. Actual newer-name refusal posted no additional native calls. This adds scalar evidence, not naming-plan or coupled preservation qualification.
limits: Only one exact-local physical Aux action is qualified here. This is not a whole naming plan, coupled Arrange/Mixer action, swap planner, batch executor, Saga journal, idempotency layer or universal duplicate-name policy.

The historical cache population is intentionally not rewritten as a fresh observation. Same-source causal reference rebinding and reread_required do not refresh or qualify the population/plan footprint.

Unknown coupling and unobserved preservation domains remain unqualified. These unchanged instrumented repeats do not erase or attribute the earlier primitive's playhead drift or the Arrange adapter's earlier fader drift.
English UI evidence is bounded to this stopped fixture and retained objects. It does not establish all locales, unsupported host versions, hidden strips, replacement objects or all target kinds.
There is no public MCP command, clean publication-head native qualification, hosted CI result, coverage promotion, release or notarization claim for this private adapter. Issue #968 remains open.
